subject: VeloxAI capacity: demand snapshot & targeted probing
messages:
From: Holly Lane <holly.lane@veloxai.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@veloxai.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: VeloxAI — demand snapshot for dedicated capacity

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the questionnaire — attaching the traces and a short CSV that summarizes our SLA targets and a handful of example prompts. Below is a compact snapshot of our traffic profile to help your sizing pass. Happy to expand if you need more granularity.

Key numbers:
- Active concurrent sessions (typical): 240 (web chat UI), 75 (API ingestion workloads).
- Median session turns: 1–3 prompts.
- Median prompt length: ~220 tokens. Median model response: ~580 tokens.
- Average tokens per request (prompt + response): ~800 tokens.
- Sustained peak: ~110 qps (5-minute sustained window).
- Micro-bursts: up to ~380 qps sustained for 20–40s during promotional events.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: ~45% of chat requests are streaming (partial outputs), the rest are single-response calls.
- Embeddings: background batch jobs process ~1,200 documents/hour (avg 1,800 tokens/doc). These run in off-peak windows but account for ~18% of total token volume when active.
- Latency SLOs: we want p95 streaming-start < 600ms and p95 full-response < 1500ms for non-streaming chat.
- Retention/compliance: we need 90-day audit logs, VPC connectivity, and support for customer-managed KMS.
- Growth expectation: ~2x total qps over the next 9 months with seasonal spikes.

Files attached: velox_traces_202811.zip (sample 72-hour trace, anonymized), velox_sla_workload.csv (high-level SLA/endpoint summary), example_prompts_nd_responses.txt (variety of prompt/response shapes).

Questions for Redwood: can you provide the expected GPU footprint (rough SKU map) and a short write-up of tradeoffs (e.g., more GPUs with more quantization vs fewer GPUs with fp16)? Also let us know recommended reserved commit levels vs burst options.

Thanks — feel free to loop anyone else in.

Holly Lane
Head of ML Infrastructure
VeloxAI
holly.lane@veloxai.com
+1 (415) 555-0138

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Holly Lane <holly.lane@veloxai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Nov 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VeloxAI — demand snapshot for dedicated capacity

Holly — really helpful, thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments. A couple quick clarifying items so we size to the right constraints:

1) Endpoint breakdown: can you confirm percent-split by route (chat REST, chat streaming, embeddings batch, reranking)? The CSV looks close but we want the 24h percent share by qps.
2) Session reuse: are users commonly reusing an open session (long-lived KV cache) or are most sessions ephemeral and single-shot? That changes KV cache sizing and memory policies.
3) Tokenization: are the token counts pre-tokenization or measured from your tokenizer? If pre-tokenization we should request a small sample to avoid under/overestimating.
4) Sampling/regeneration patterns: what percentage of requests do partial-regenerations/edits (i.e., multiple model calls per user action)?
5) Embeddings infrastructure: do you want embeddings handled on the same dedicated fleet or to run in a separate batch cluster? Any SLA on embeddings latency?
6) Security: confirm VPC + customer KMS requirement and whether SOC2 attestation is required for credentialing prior to a pilot.

Next steps: we recommend a 60-minute sizing workshop where we walk through the traces and map tokens -> GPU seconds. Are you available Wed 11/15 at 09:00 PT or Thu 11/16 at 11:00 PT? If Wed works we will invite Karthik and Rishi to focus on quantization and kernel assumptions.

FYI @Marissa: once we have the per-route split and a sample tokenized trace, I can produce a first-pass GPU-map (ballpark SKUs and committed capacity recommendation).

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Holly Lane <holly.lane@veloxai.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Reyes <carlos.reyes@veloxai.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: VeloxAI — demand snapshot for dedicated capacity

Laura / team,

Thanks — answers inline below and I attached a timestamped 24-hour tokenized trace in the zip (velox_traces_202811.zip) and a short Drive folder with higher-fidelity examples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1VeloxSamples

1) Endpoint split (24h qps share): chat streaming 38%, chat non-streaming 22%, embeddings batch 25%, reranking/other 15%.
2) Session reuse: web sessions are sticky (approx 60% of web sessions reuse an open session for 2–15 minutes). API calls are mostly ephemeral.
3) Tokenization: the CSV uses counts from our tokenizer (so they are tokenized counts). The zip includes a sample converter script.
4) Regeneration: ~9% of chat calls are a follow-up re-generate within 5s.
5) Embeddings: we prefer embeddings to be separate (batch window); latency SLA for embeddings is soft (minutes). Keep them off the low-latency dedicated lane unless you recommend otherwise for cost reasons.
6) Security: yes — VPC + customer KMS required. SOC2 report will be needed for procurement.

We are leaning toward a reserved commit for predictable cost but want to understand what a reasonable starting commit looks like (in terms of GPUs and committed throughput). Also curious about fallback options (hosted burst) — can Redwood automatically overflow to hosted capacity for very short spikes?

I'll confirm Wed 11/15 09:00 PT for the workshop. Attaching the CSV and a small sample of prompts for context.

Holly

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Holly Lane <holly.lane@veloxai.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Nov 2028 15:27:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: VeloxAI — demand snapshot for dedicated capacity — internal notes + next steps

Team — forwarding the Velox traffic snapshot and notes from the 11/15 workshop (recorded). Summary and suggested immediate actions:

Summary from traces:
- 24h qps shape: steady baseline ~45 qps with promotional micro-bursts to 380 qps (30–45s).
- Token mix: median 800 tokens/request; heavy tail to ~6k tokens for long-form generation (rare).
- Session stickiness: web chat has ~60% reuse; that implies sustained KV cache residency for a subset.
- Embeddings are explicitly separable and should run on a separate batch plane.

First-pass GPU footprint (ballpark):
- Option A (aggressive quantization): 6 x H100-80GB (q4_0/q2_K mixed) to meet baseline + 1.5x burst headroom with autoscale; assumes our optimized kernel path and prefix caching.
- Option B (conservative/fp16): 12 x A100-80GB (fp16) to meet the same SLOs without quantization risk; higher unit cost but simpler validation for customers needing strict determinism.

Assumptions and open items for Rishi/Karthik:
- Rishi: confirm qps->GPU-second conversion using the H100 kernel latency numbers for a median 800-token request (include streaming-start cost vs full-token cost). Also call out memory for KV cache sizing assuming 60% session reuse.
- Karthik: recommend burst policy (cold vs warm autoscale), preferred canary cadence, and whether Redwood-hosted overflow is safe as a short-term fallback for 30–60s micro-bursts. Also confirm recommended network egress/ingress architecture for VPC peering.

Next steps for Marissa: draft a proposal with two commitment options (Option A and Option B above) and include estimated monthly committed GPU-hours, a short pricing delta for hosted-burst overflow, and an implementation timeline for pilot -> production. Also attach SOC2 and KMS onboarding checklist to the proposal.

Holly — we'll share the formal proposal early next week. For now the two SKU maps above should give you a sense of tradeoffs; we'll finalize after Rishi's latency conversion and a short calibration test (30-minute profiler run).

Thanks — Laura

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
